verses.text: This is the story of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. After the flood, these 3 men had sons.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
The people of the lands near the sea came from these sons. They spread out into their own lands. Each family had its own language and its own nation.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabtecha. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush also had a son named Nimrod. Nimrod became the first great and powerful ruler on the earth.
Nimrod was a mighty hunter before the LORD. That is why people say: Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.
Nimrod's kingdom began with the cities of Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh. These cities were in the land of Shinar.
From that land Asshur went out and built the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth, and Calah.
Asshur also built Resen, between Nineveh and Calah. Resen was a great city.
Mizraim was the father of the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim.
Mizraim was also the father of the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, and the Caphtorim. The Philistines came from the Casluhim.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his oldest son, and of Heth.
Canaan was also the father of the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.
Canaan was also the father of the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
Canaan was also the father of the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the families of the Canaanites spread out.
The land of the Canaanites reached from Sidon toward Gerar, as far as Gaza. It also reached toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham. They are listed by their families, languages, lands, and nations.
Shem also had sons. Shem was the father of all the sons of Eber. Shem was also the older brother of Japheth.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arphaxad was the father of Salah. Salah was the father of Eber.
Eber had 2 sons. One was named Peleg, because the earth was divided in his time. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
Joktan was also the father of Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
Joktan was also the father of Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.
Joktan was also the father of Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Their land reached from Mesha to Sephar, in the mountain land of the east.
These are the sons of Shem. They are listed by their families, languages, lands, and nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noah. They are listed by their family lines and nations. After the flood, the nations of the earth spread out from these families.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: At that time the whole earth had 1 language. Everyone used the same words.
As people traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar. They settled there.
They said to each other: Come, let us make bricks and bake them hard. They used bricks for stone and tar to hold the bricks together.
Then they said: Come, let us build a city for ourselves. Let us build a tower with its top in the sky. Let us make a name for ourselves. Then we will not be scattered over the whole earth.
The LORD came down to see the city and the tower. The people were building them.
The LORD said: Look, these people are united. They all speak the same language. This is only the beginning of what they will do. Now nothing they plan to do will be too hard for them.
The LORD also said: Come, let Us go down and mix up their language. Then they will not understand each other.
So the LORD scattered them from there over the whole earth. They stopped building the city.
That is why the city was named Babel. There the LORD mixed up the language of the whole earth. From there the LORD scattered the people over the whole earth.
This is the story of the family of Shem. When Shem was 100 years old, he had a son named Arphaxad. This was 2 years after the flood.
After Arphaxad was born, Shem lived 500 more years. Shem had other sons and daughters.
When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he had a son named Salah.
After Salah was born, Arphaxad lived 403 more years. Arphaxad had other sons and daughters.
When Salah was 30 years old, he had a son named Eber.
After Eber was born, Salah lived 403 more years. Salah had other sons and daughters.
When Eber was 34 years old, he had a son named Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived 430 more years. Eber had other sons and daughters.
When Peleg was 30 years old, he had a son named Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived 209 more years. Peleg had other sons and daughters.
When Reu was 32 years old, he had a son named Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived 207 more years. Reu had other sons and daughters.
When Serug was 30 years old, he had a son named Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived 200 more years. Serug had other sons and daughters.
When Nahor was 29 years old, he had a son named Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived 119 more years. Nahor had other sons and daughters.
When Terah was 70 years old, he began to have sons: Abram, Nahor and Haran.
This is the story of the family of Terah. Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. Haran was the father of Lot.
Haran died in the land where he was born, Ur of the Chaldeans. His father Terah was still alive.
Abram and Nahor each married. Abram's wife was named Sarai. Nahor's wife was named Milcah. Milcah was the daughter of Haran. Haran was also the father of Iscah.
Sarai could not have children.
Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot and his daughter-in-law Sarai, Abram's wife. They left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came to the town of Haran and settled there.
Terah lived 205 years. Then Terah died in Haran.

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 4 ('whose top may reach unto heaven') is rendered 'with its top in the sky'; verse 3 'slime' is rendered 'tar'; verse 7 keeps 'Us' capitalized as in Genesis 1:26; the ages in verses 10-25 follow the KJV numbers (the genealogy has no totals, so none are added); verse 26 'begat Abram, Nahor and Haran' is rendered 'began to have sons'.

verses.text: The LORD said to Abram: You must leave your land. Go away from it and from your family and the house of your father. I will show you where you must go.
I will build a great nation from you. I will bless you and make your name famous. People will use your name to bless other people.
I will bless those who bless you. I will curse those who curse you. I will use you to bless all the people on earth.
So Abram left Haran just like the LORD said, and Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran.
Abram took his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot. He took all the possessions and servants they had gathered in Haran. Then they set out for the land of Canaan.
Abram walked from one side of the land to the other side. At that time the Canaanite people lived in the land. Abram went to the town of Shechem, to the big tree of Moreh.
The LORD appeared to Abram. The LORD said: I will give this land to your children and your family. Then Abram built an altar to the LORD there.
Then Abram left Shechem and traveled to the mountains east of Bethel. Abram set up his tent there. Bethel was to the west, and Ai was to the east. Abram built an altar there to worship the LORD.
Later, Abram took his tents and traveled south, toward the Negev.
Then there was very little food in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a while.
When they came near Egypt, Abram said to his wife Sarai: I know you are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, Sarai, they will say: This is his wife. Then they will kill me, but they will let you live.
Please say that you are my sister. Then things will go well for me because of you. Because of you, my life will be saved.
When Abram and Sarai came into the land of Egypt, the people of Egypt saw how beautiful Sarai was.
Pharaoh's officials saw Sarai. They told Pharaoh how beautiful she was. Sarai was taken into Pharaoh's palace.
Pharaoh was good to Abram because Pharaoh thought that Sarai was Abram's sister. Pharaoh gave Abram sheep, oxen, donkeys, slaves and camels.
But the LORD struck Pharaoh and Pharaoh's household with severe sicknesses because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Then Pharaoh called Abram. Pharaoh asked: What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me that Sarai is your wife?
Why did you say: She is my sister? I took her to be my wife. Now here is your wife. Take her and go.
Pharaoh gave orders to his men about Abram. They sent Abram away with his wife and everything he had.

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: Abram left Egypt and went to the Negev in the south of Canaan. He took his wife Sarai and everything he had. Lot went with them.
Abram was very rich. Abram had many sheep, goats and oxen, and Abram also had a lot of silver and gold.
Abram continued traveling around. Abram went back to Bethel. Abram went to the place between the city of Bethel and Hai where Abram and his family had camped before.
The first time that Abram had been there, Abram had built an altar. Now Abram called on the name of the LORD at the altar.
Lot was with Abram and Lot also had sheep, goats, oxen and tents.
The land could not feed all their animals. They had too many animals to stay together.
Then the shepherds of Abram and the shepherds of Lot started to fight. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the land.
Abram said to Lot: We are family. Let there be no fighting between you and me. Let there be no fighting between my shepherds and your shepherds.
This land is big enough. It will be better if we separate. If you go to the left, then I will go to the right. If you go to the right, then I will go to the left. Lot, you can choose.

Lot looked and saw the whole Jordan Valley. It had plenty of water all the way to Zoar. It was like the Garden of the LORD and like the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
So Lot chose to live in the Jordan Valley. The 2 men separated, and Lot began traveling east.
Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. Lot lived in the towns of the valley. Lot put up his tents near the city of Sodom.
The people of Sodom were very wicked. They sinned greatly against the LORD.
After Abram and Lot had separated, the LORD said to Abram: You must look around you, to the north, to the south, to the east and to the west.
I will give you and your family all the land that you can see. This land will be your land and your family's land forever.
I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth. If anyone can count the dust of the earth, they can count your descendants.
Walk through the whole land, its length and its width. I will give it to you.
Then Abram moved his tents. Abram went to stay near the big trees of Mamre near the city of Hebron. There Abram built an altar to worship the LORD.

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: In those days, Amraphel was king of Shinar. Arioch was king of Ellasar. Chedorlaomer was king of Elam. Tidal was king of Goiim.

These 4 kings made war against 5 other kings. They fought Bera king of Sodom and Birsha king of Gomorrah. They also fought Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All 5 of these kings joined their armies in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea.
For 12 years these 5 kings had served Chedorlaomer. In the 13th year they rebelled.
In the 14th year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came. They defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim. They defeated the Zuzim in Ham. They defeated the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim.
They also defeated the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as El Paran by the desert.
Then they turned back and came to En Mishpat, which is Kadesh. They defeated the whole land of the Amalekites. They also defeated the Amorites who lived in Hazazon Tamar.
Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim and Bela, which is Zoar, marched out. They lined up for battle in the Valley of Siddim.
They fought against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar. It was 4 kings against 5.
The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away, and some of their men fell into the pits. The rest ran to the mountains.
The enemy took all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah. Then they left.
They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, who lived in Sodom. They took everything Lot owned.
A man who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living near the big trees that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner had an agreement to help Abram.
Abram heard that his nephew had been captured. Abram called out his 318 trained men who were born in his house. Abram chased the enemy as far as Dan.
That night Abram divided his men into groups and attacked. They chased the enemy to Hobah, north of Damascus.
Abram brought back all the goods. He brought back his nephew Lot and Lot's goods. He also brought back the women and the other people.
Abram defeated Chedorlaomer and the kings with him. Then Abram returned. The king of Sodom went out to meet Abram in the Valley of Shaveh, also called the King's Valley.
Melchizedek, the king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. Melchizedek was a priest of God Most High.
Melchizedek blessed Abram and said: May God Most High, who made heaven and earth, bless Abram.
Praise God Most High, who has put your enemies in your hands. Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram: Give me the people. You may keep the goods.
Abram said to the king of Sodom: I have raised my hand and sworn to the LORD, God Most High, who made heaven and earth.
I will not take anything of yours, not even a thread or a sandal strap. Then you cannot say: I made Abram rich.
I will take nothing but what my young men have eaten. But let Aner, Eshcol and Mamre take their share, because they went with me.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'king of nations' (verse 1) is 'king of Goiim' (a place name); 'brother' in verses 12-16 is rendered 'nephew'; 'Almighty/most high God' is 'God Most High'; 'tithes' is 'a tenth'; the Salt Sea is the Dead Sea; verses 19 and 22 'possessor of heaven and earth' is rendered 'made heaven and earth'.

verses.text: After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision. The LORD said: Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield. I am your very great reward.
Abram said: Lord GOD, what can You give me? I have no children. The man who will receive my house is Eliezer of Damascus.
Abram also said: You have given me no children. A servant born in my house will receive everything I have.
Then the word of the LORD came to Abram: This servant will not receive what is yours. Your own son will receive it.
The LORD took Abram outside and said: Look up at the sky. Count the stars, if you can. Then the LORD said: That is how many descendants you will have.
Abram believed the LORD. The LORD counted Abram's faith as doing what is right.
The LORD said to Abram: I am the LORD. I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans. I did this to give you this land.
Abram said: Lord GOD, how can I know that I will receive it?
The LORD said to Abram: Bring Me a young cow, a goat and a ram, each 3 years old. Bring Me also a dove and a young pigeon.
Abram brought all these animals. Abram cut each animal in half. He laid the halves across from each other. But he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds that eat dead bodies came down on the animals. Abram drove them away.
When the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep. Then terror and thick darkness came over him.
The LORD said to Abram: You can be sure of this. Your descendants will live in a land that is not theirs. They will serve the people there. Those people will be cruel to them for 400 years.
But I will punish the nation they serve. Afterward your descendants will leave with great riches.
You will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.
In the 4th generation your descendants will come back here. The Amorites have not yet sinned enough to be punished.
When the sun went down, it was dark. A smoking fire pot and a burning torch passed between the pieces.
On that day the LORD made an agreement with Abram: I have given this land to your descendants. It reaches from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.
This land includes the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites and the Kadmonites.
It includes the land of the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Rephaim.
It includes the land of the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites and the Jebusites.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 4 'out of thine own bowels' is rendered 'your own son'; verse 6 'righteousness' is rendered 'doing what is right'; verse 8 'Lord GOD' follows the house rule; verses 10-17 (the animal pieces and the fire pot) and 19-21 (lists) are literal.

verses.text: Sarai, Abram's wife, had no children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram: The LORD has kept me from having children. Please sleep with my servant. Maybe I can have a family through her. Abram agreed to what Sarai said.
Abram had lived in Canaan for 10 years. Then Sarai took her Egyptian servant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar knew she was pregnant, she looked down on Sarai.
Sarai said to Abram: This wrong done to me is your fault. I gave my servant to you. Now that she is pregnant, she looks down on me. May the LORD judge between you and me.
Abram said to Sarai: Your servant is in your hands. Do to her what you think is best. Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that Hagar ran away.
The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert. The spring was on the road to Shur.
The angel said: Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from? Where are you going? Hagar said: I am running away from my mistress Sarai.
The angel of the LORD said to her: Go back to your mistress. Obey her.
The angel of the LORD also said: I will give you so many descendants that no one can count them.
The angel of the LORD said: You are pregnant, and you will have a son. Name him Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your cry of trouble.
Ishmael will be a wild man. His hand will be against everyone, and everyone's hand will be against him. Ishmael will live near all his brothers.
Hagar gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: You are the God who sees me. She said: Have I really seen the One who sees me, even here?
So the well was named Beer Lahai Roi, which means The well of the Living One who sees me. It is between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar had a son for Abram. Abram named the son Ishmael.
Abram was 86 years old when Hagar had Ishmael.

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'go in unto' (verses 2 and 4) is rendered 'sleep with'; verse 12 'wild man' is Hebrew 'wild donkey of a man' and 'in the presence of' is rendered 'near'; verse 13 (the name Hagar gives God and her question) is hard Hebrew; verse 14 adds the meaning of the well's name.

verses.text: When Abram was 99 years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said: I am God Almighty. Walk with Me and live a blameless life.
I will make My agreement with you. I will give you a great many descendants.
Abram bowed down with his face to the ground. Then God spoke to him.
God said: This is My agreement with you. You will be the father of many nations.
Your name will no longer be Abram. Your name will be Abraham. I have made you the father of many nations.
I will give you very many descendants. Nations will come from you. Kings will come from you.
I will make My agreement with you and with your descendants after you. It will last for all time. I will be your God and the God of your descendants.
I will give you and your descendants the land where you now live as a stranger. All the land of Canaan will be yours forever. I will be their God.
God said to Abraham: You must keep My agreement. You and your descendants after you must keep it through all time.
This is My agreement with you and your descendants. You must keep it. Every male among you must be circumcised.
You must circumcise every male, which means cutting off the foreskin. This will be the sign of the agreement between Me and you.
Every baby boy must be circumcised when he is 8 days old. This includes boys born in your house and boys you bought from foreigners. It includes every generation.
Every male born in your house or bought with your money must be circumcised. My agreement will be marked on your bodies. It will last forever.
Any male who is not circumcised will be cut off from his people. He has broken My agreement.
God said to Abraham: Do not call your wife Sarai any longer. Her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her. I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her.
Abraham bowed down with his face to the ground, and he laughed. He said to himself: Can a man who is 100 years old have a child? Can Sarah, who is 90 years old, have a baby?
Abraham said to God: I wish Ishmael could live under Your blessing.
God said: No, your wife Sarah will have a son for you. You will name him Isaac. I will make My agreement with Isaac. It will last forever for him and his descendants.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I have blessed him. I will give him many descendants. He will father 12 princes. I will make him a great nation.
But I will make My agreement with Isaac. Sarah will give birth to him about this time next year.
When God finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
On that same day, Abraham took his son Ishmael and every male in his house. This included those born in his house and those he had bought. Abraham circumcised them, as God had told him.
Abraham was 99 years old when he was circumcised.
Ishmael was 13 years old when he was circumcised.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on that same day.
All the men of Abraham's house were circumcised with him. This included those born in his house and those bought from foreigners.

17.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'covenant' is 'agreement'; 'Almighty God' (verse 1) is 'God Almighty'; 'circumcised' is kept as a Bible word and explained in verse 11; verse 17 'Shall a child be born' is rendered as two questions; verse 18 is a prayer for Ishmael.

verses.text: The LORD appeared to Abraham near the trees of Mamre. Abraham was sitting in front of the door of his tent. It was very hot.
Abraham looked up and suddenly saw 3 men standing not far away. Abraham ran from his tent to meet the men and bowed down with his face to the ground.
Abraham said: My Lord, if I have found favor with You, please do not go past my tent. Please stay for a short while.
I will bring you some water, and then you can wash your feet. You can rest here under this tree.
I will also bring you some bread and when you have eaten enough, you can go on. I am happy that you have come to me, your servant. Then the men said to Abraham: Yes, you can do what you have said.
Abraham quickly went to Sarah in the tent and told her: prepare enough flour for three loaves of bread.
Then Abraham ran to his cattle and chose the best young calf. Abraham gave the calf to a servant and told the servant to kill it and cook it.
Abraham brought some cream and milk and the meat of the calf and Abraham gave it to the 3 men. They ate and Abraham stood with them under the tree.
Then the 3 men asked Abraham: Where is your wife, Sarah? Abraham answered and said: She is here in the tent.
One of the men said to Abraham: I will come back next year and then Sarah will have a baby boy. Sarah was in the tent and heard what the LORD said.
Abraham and Sarah were very old. Sarah was too old to have a baby.
Sarah laughed and said to herself: I am too old. I cannot have a baby now, and my husband is old too.
The LORD said to Abraham: Why did Sarah laugh and say, Can I really have a baby when I am old?
I am the Lord. I can do anything that I want to do. I will come back next year at the time that I have said, and then Sarah will have a son.
Sarah was afraid. Sarah lied and said: I did not laugh. But the Lord said: Yes, you did.
The 3 men wanted to go. They looked at the city of Sodom and Abraham walked with them to send them on their way.
The LORD said: Should I keep secret from Abraham what I am about to do?
Abraham will become a great and powerful nation, and all the nations on earth will be blessed because of Abraham.

I chose Abraham so that Abraham will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD, doing what is right and just. Then I will give Abraham everything that I have promised.
The LORD said: The outcry against the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah is very great, and their sin is very serious.
I will go down now to see whether the people there have done as bad as the outcry says. If not, I will know.
Then the other 2 of the men started to walk to the city of Sodom. But the Lord did not go but stayed with Abraham.
Abraham approached and said: Will you destroy the righteous along with the wicked?
Suppose there are fifty righteous people in the city. Will you destroy the city and not spare it for the sake of the fifty righteous people in it?
Far be it from you to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, treating the righteous and the wicked the same way! Should not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?
The LORD said: If I find fifty righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake.
Then Abraham said, compared to you, Lord, I am only dust and ashes. But let me bother you again and ask you this question.

Abraham said, Suppose there are only forty-five righteous people instead of fifty. Will you destroy the whole city for the lack of five? God answered: If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy the city.
Abraham spoke again: Suppose forty are found there. The LORD said: I will not destroy it, for the sake of the forty.
Abraham said: Lord, please do not be angry with me if I speak. Suppose thirty are found there. The LORD said: I will not destroy it, if I find thirty there.
Then Abraham said: Let me be so bold as to speak to the Lord again. Suppose twenty are found there. The LORD said: I will not destroy it, for the sake of the twenty.
Then Abraham said: Lord, please don't be angry with me. Let me speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there. The LORD said: I will not destroy it, for the sake of the ten.
After the Lord had talked to Abraham, the LORD went away, and Abraham went to his home.

18.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: That evening the 2 angels came to Sodom. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them. He bowed down with his face to the ground.
Lot said: Sirs, please come to my house. Stay the night and wash your feet. Then you can get up early and go on your way. The angels said: No. We will spend the night in the street.
But Lot urged them strongly. So they went with him into his house. Lot prepared a meal and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.
Before they went to bed, all the men of Sodom surrounded the house. Young and old, men from every part of the city came.
They called to Lot: Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them.
Lot went outside and shut the door behind him.
Lot said: My brothers, please do not do this evil thing.
Listen, I have 2 daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you. Do to them whatever you want. But do not do anything to these men, because they are guests under my roof.

The men said: Get out of the way. They said: This man came here as a stranger, and now he wants to judge us. We will treat you worse than them. They pushed hard against Lot and came near to breaking down the door.
But the 2 angels reached out and pulled Lot back into the house. They shut the door.
The angels made the men outside the door blind, both young and old. The men were worn out trying to find the door.
The angels said to Lot: Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else in the city? Bring them out of this place.
We are going to destroy this place. The cry against its people has become great before the LORD. The LORD has sent us to destroy it.

Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were going to marry his daughters. Lot said: Get up and leave this place, because the LORD will destroy this city. But the sons-in-law thought Lot was joking.
At dawn the angels urged Lot: Get up. Take your wife and your 2 daughters who are here. Then you will not be swept away when the city is punished.
Lot still hesitated. So the angels took Lot, his wife and his 2 daughters by the hand, because the LORD was merciful to them. The angels led them out and left them outside the city.
When they were outside, one angel said: Run for your lives. Do not look back. Do not stop anywhere in the valley. Run to the mountains, or you will be swept away.
Lot said to them: No, Lord, please.
You have been kind to me and have shown great mercy by saving my life. But I cannot run to the mountains. The disaster will catch me, and I will die.
Look, that town over there is close enough to run to. It is a small town. Please let me escape there. It is only a small place. Then my life will be saved.
The angel said to Lot: I will grant this request too. I will not destroy the town you spoke about.
Hurry. Run there, because I cannot do anything until you arrive. That is why the town was named Zoar.
The sun had risen over the land when Lot reached Zoar.
Then the LORD rained burning sulfur down on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came from the LORD out of heaven.
The LORD destroyed those cities and the whole valley. The LORD destroyed all the people in the cities and everything that grew on the ground.
Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Early the next morning, Abraham went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
Abraham looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the valley. He saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the valley, God remembered Abraham. God brought Lot out of the disaster when God destroyed the cities where Lot lived.
Lot was afraid to stay in Zoar. So Lot and his 2 daughters went up into the mountains and lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger: Our father is old. There is no man in the land to marry us, as is the custom everywhere.
Come, let us make our father drink wine. Then we will sleep with him, so that we can have children from our father's family.
That night they made their father drink wine. The older daughter went in and slept with her father. Lot did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day the older daughter said to the younger: Last night I slept with my father. Let us make him drink wine again tonight. Then you go in and sleep with him, so that we can have children from our father's family.
That night they made their father drink wine again. The younger daughter went in and slept with him. Lot did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter had a son and named him Moab. Moab is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter also had a son and named him Ben Ammi. Ben Ammi is the father of the Ammonites to this day.

19.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Hard chapter: verses 5 and 8 (the crowd and Lot's offer of his daughters) and verses 31-38 (Lot's daughters) are rendered plainly but faithfully and need careful review. Verse 18 'my Lord' is kept as 'Lord'; verse 21 is the angel speaking for the LORD; 'brimstone' is 'burning sulfur'.

verses.text: Abraham moved from there toward the Negev. He lived between Kadesh and Shur. Then he stayed for a while in Gerar.
Abraham said of his wife Sarah: She is my sister. So Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream at night. God said: You are a dead man because of the woman you have taken. She is another man's wife.
Abimelech had not gone near her. He said: Lord, will You kill a nation that is innocent?
Did Abraham not say to me: She is my sister? Sarah herself said: He is my brother. I did this with an honest heart and clean hands.
God said to Abimelech in the dream: Yes, I know you did this with an honest heart. I kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now give the man his wife back. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you so that you will live. If you do not give her back, you will surely die, you and everyone who belongs to you.
Early the next morning Abimelech called all his servants. He told them everything that had happened. The men were very afraid.
Then Abimelech called Abraham and said: What have you done to us? How have I wronged you? You have brought a great sin on me and my kingdom. You have done to me what should never be done.
Abimelech also said to Abraham: What made you do this?
Abraham said: I thought: No one in this place fears God. They will kill me to get my wife.
Also, she really is my sister. She is the daughter of my father, but not of my mother. She became my wife.
When God made me leave my father's house and wander, I said to Sarah: Do this kindness for me. Everywhere we go, say that I am your brother.
Then Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, oxen, and male and female servants. Abimelech gave Sarah, Abraham's wife, back to him.
Abimelech said: My land is before you. Live wherever you like.
Abimelech said to Sarah: I have given your brother 1,000 pieces of silver. This is to make everything right with you and everyone with you. You are cleared before everyone.
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his female servants. They could have children again.
The LORD had closed every womb in the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

20.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 4 'Lord' is Adonai; verse 16 ('a covering of the eyes') is hard Hebrew and is rendered by its meaning; verse 14 gives Sarah back to Abraham.

verses.text: The LORD cared for Sarah as He had said. The LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and had a son for Abraham in his old age. It was at the exact time God had told him.
Abraham named the son Sarah had for him Isaac.
When Isaac was 8 days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded.
Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.
Sarah said: God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.
Sarah also said: Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse babies? But I have given him a son in his old age.
The child grew and was weaned. On the day Isaac was weaned, Abraham gave a great feast.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian making fun of Isaac. Hagar had borne this son to Abraham.
Sarah said to Abraham: Send away this servant woman and her son. The son of this servant will not share what you leave with my son Isaac.
This made Abraham very upset because Ishmael was his son.
But God said to Abraham: Do not be upset about the boy and your servant. Listen to everything Sarah tells you. Your descendants will come through Isaac.
I will also make a nation from the son of the servant, because he is your son too.
Early the next morning Abraham took bread and a bottle of water. Abraham put them on Hagar's shoulder and sent her away with the boy. Hagar wandered in the desert of Beersheba.
When the water in the bottle was gone, Hagar put the boy under a bush.
Hagar went and sat down about a bowshot away. She said: I cannot watch the boy die. She sat there and cried out loud.
God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven: What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy crying where he lies.
Get up. Lift the boy and hold him by the hand. I will make him a great nation.
Then God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the bottle with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy as he grew up. Ishmael lived in the desert and became an archer.
Ishmael lived in the desert of Paran. His mother found a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham: God is with you in everything you do.
Now swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me, my children or my descendants. Show me and this land where you have lived as a stranger the same kindness I have shown you.
Abraham said: I swear.
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had taken by force.
Abimelech said: I do not know who did this. You did not tell me, and I did not hear about it until today.
Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and oxen, and the two men made an agreement.
Abraham set 7 young female lambs apart from the flock.
Abimelech asked Abraham: Why have you set these 7 lambs apart?
Abraham said: Please accept these 7 lambs from me. They will show that I dug this well.
So that place was named Beersheba, because the two men swore an oath there.
They made an agreement at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, went back to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he called on the name of the LORD, the God who lives forever.
Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

21.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: verse 9 'mocking' (the KJV names no one; rendered 'making fun of Isaac'); verse 33 'grove' is a tamarisk tree; 'covenant' is 'agreement'; 'Beersheba' means well of the oath (or of 7).

verses.text: Some time later God tested Abraham. God said: Abraham. Abraham said: Here I am.
God said: Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love. Go to the land of Moriah. There offer him as a burnt offering on a mountain that I will show you.
Early the next morning Abraham saddled his donkey. He took 2 of his young men and his son Isaac. He cut wood for the burnt offering. Then Abraham set out for the place God had told him about.
On the 3rd day Abraham looked up and saw the place far away.
Abraham said to his young men: Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there and worship. Then we will come back to you.
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac. Abraham carried the fire and the knife. The two of them walked on together.
Isaac said to his father Abraham: Father. Abraham said: Here I am, my son. Isaac said: We have the fire and the wood. But where is the lamb for the burnt offering?
Abraham said: My son, God will provide the lamb for the burnt offering. The two of them walked on together.
They came to the place God had told Abraham about. Abraham built an altar there and laid the wood on it. Then Abraham tied up his son Isaac and laid Isaac on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.
But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven: Abraham, Abraham. Abraham said: Here I am.
The angel said: Do not lay your hand on the boy. Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not held back your son, your only son, from Me.
Abraham looked up and saw a ram behind him. The ram's horns were caught in a bush. Abraham went and took the ram. He offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham named that place The LORD Will Provide. To this day people say: On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time.
The angel said: I swear by Myself, says the LORD. You have done this. You have not held back your son, your only son.
So I will greatly bless you. I will give you as many descendants as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take the cities of their enemies.
All the nations of the earth will be blessed through your descendants, because you have obeyed Me.
Abraham went back to his young men. They got up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
Some time later Abraham was told: Milcah has also had children for your brother Nahor.
Huz was the oldest son. Buz was his brother. Kemuel was the father of Aram.
The others were Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel.
Bethuel was the father of Rebekah. Milcah had these 8 sons for Abraham's brother Nahor.
Nahor also had a second wife named Reumah. She had sons named Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

22.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'tempt' (verse 1) is 'tested'; verse 12 has the angel speaking as God ('from Me'); verse 14 'Jehovahjireh' is rendered 'The LORD Will Provide'; verse 16 'concubine' (verse 24) is 'second wife'.

verses.text: Sarah lived 127 years.
Sarah died in Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham went to mourn and cry for Sarah.
Abraham got up from beside his wife's body. He spoke to the Hittites.
Abraham said: I am a stranger and a guest among you. Let me have a piece of land among you for a burial place, so that I can bury my wife.
The Hittites answered Abraham.
They said: Sir, listen to us. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the best of our graves. None of us will refuse you a grave for your dead.
Abraham stood up and bowed down to the people of the land, the Hittites.
Abraham said to them: If you are willing to let me bury my dead, please listen to me. Ask Ephron son of Zohar for me.
Ask him to sell me the cave of Machpelah, at the end of his field. I will pay him the full price in front of you, so that I will own it as a burial place.
Ephron was sitting among the Hittites. Ephron answered Abraham in front of all the Hittites who came to the city gate.
Ephron said: No, sir, listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave in it. I give it to you in front of my people. Bury your dead.
Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
Abraham spoke to Ephron in front of the people: Please listen to me. I will pay the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I can bury my dead there.
Ephron answered Abraham.
Ephron said: Sir, listen to me. The land is worth 400 shekels of silver. That is nothing between you and me. Bury your dead.
Abraham agreed with Ephron. Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver he had named in front of the Hittites, 400 shekels of silver, by the merchants' standard.
Ephron's field in Machpelah, east of Mamre, was sold. This included the field, the cave in it and all the trees within its borders.
It became Abraham's property in front of the Hittites and everyone who came to the city gate.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah, east of Mamre. That is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
So the field and the cave in it became Abraham's property as a burial place, bought from the Hittites.

23.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'sons of Heth' is 'the Hittites'; verse 4 'give me' is rendered 'Let me have' because Abraham pays in full; verses 3, 5 and 14 are short lead-in sentences because the KJV ends them with 'saying'; a shekel is about 0.4 ounce of silver.

verses.text: Abraham was now very old. The LORD had blessed Abraham in every way.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, who was in charge of everything Abraham owned: Put your hand under my thigh.
I want you to swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and earth, that you will not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live.
Instead, go to my own country and my own relatives. Choose a wife for my son Isaac there.
The servant said to Abraham: Maybe the woman will not want to follow me to this land. Should I take your son back to the land you came from?
Abraham said to him: Be careful. Do not take my son back there.

The LORD, the God of heaven, took me from my father's house and from the land where I was born. He spoke to me and swore: I will give this land to your descendants. The LORD will send His angel ahead of you, and you will get a wife for my son from there.
If the woman will not follow you, then you are free from this oath. But do not take my son back there.
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to him about this.
The servant took 10 of his master's camels and all kinds of good gifts from his master. He set out for Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel down outside the city by a well of water. It was evening, the time when women come out to draw water.
He prayed: LORD, God of my master Abraham, please give me success today. Show kindness to my master Abraham.
Look, I am standing here by the well. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let it happen like this. I will say to a young woman: Please lower your jar so I can drink. If she says: Drink, and I will give your camels water too, let her be the one You have chosen for Your servant Isaac. Then I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.
Before the servant finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah and Nahor, Abraham's brother.
The young woman was very beautiful. She had never slept with a man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar and came up.
The servant ran to meet her and said: Please let me drink a little water from your jar.
She said: Drink, sir. She quickly lowered her jar into her hands and gave him a drink.
When she had given him a drink, she said: I will also draw water for your camels until they have had enough.
She quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw more. She drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her quietly. He wanted to know whether the LORD had made his journey a success or not.
When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold ring that weighed half a shekel. He also took 2 gold bracelets that weighed 10 shekels.
He asked: Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to stay the night?
She said: I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah and Nahor.
She also said: We have plenty of straw and feed. We also have room for you to stay.
The man bowed his head and worshiped the LORD.
He said: Praise the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. He has not stopped showing kindness and faithfulness to my master. The LORD led me on the way to the house of my master's relatives.
The young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Laban ran out to the man at the spring.
Laban had seen the ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms. He had heard his sister Rebekah say: This is what the man told me. So Laban went to the man standing by the camels at the spring.
Laban said: Come in, you who are blessed by the LORD. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.
So the man came into the house. Laban unloaded the camels and gave them straw and feed. Laban brought water to wash the man's feet and the feet of the men with him.
Food was set before the man. But he said: I will not eat until I have told you why I came. Laban said: Tell us.
The servant said: I am Abraham's servant.
The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. The LORD has given him sheep, oxen, silver, gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
Sarah, my master's wife, had a son for my master when she was old. My master has given him everything he owns.
My master made me swear. He said: Do not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live.
Go to my father's house and to my own family. Choose a wife for my son there.
I said to my master: Maybe the woman will not follow me.
He said to me: The LORD, whom I walk with, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success. You will get a wife for my son from my own family and my father's house.
Then you will be free from my oath. If you go to my family and they refuse to give her to you, you will also be free from my oath.
Today I came to the spring and prayed: LORD, God of my master Abraham, if You will make my journey a success,
Look, I am standing by the spring. When a young woman comes out to draw water, I will say: Please give me a little water from your jar.
If she says: Drink, and I will draw water for your camels too, let her be the woman the LORD has chosen for my master's son.
I had not finished praying in my heart when Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her: Please give me a drink.
She quickly lowered her jar and said: Drink, and I will give your camels water too. So I drank, and she gave the camels water too.
I asked her: Whose daughter are you? She said: I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah. Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
I bowed my head and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to get the granddaughter of my master's brother for his son.
Now tell me if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master. If not, tell me, so that I can know what to do.
Laban and Bethuel answered: This is from the LORD. We cannot say yes or no to you.
Rebekah is here. Take her and go. Let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has said.
When Abraham's servant heard this, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.
The servant brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothing and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
Then the servant and the men with him ate and drank and stayed the night. When they got up in the morning, the servant said: Send me back to my master.
Rebekah's brother and mother said: Let the young woman stay with us for 10 days or so. Then she can go.
But the servant said to them: Do not delay me. The LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so I can go to my master.
They said: Let us call the young woman and ask her.
They called Rebekah and asked her: Will you go with this man? She said: I will go.
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way with her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said: Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take the cities of their enemies.
Then Rebekah and her young women got up, rode on the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Isaac had come from the well Beer Lahai Roi. He was living in the Negev.
One evening Isaac went out to the field to think. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel.
She asked the servant: Who is that man walking in the field to meet us? The servant said: He is my master. So Rebekah took her veil and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah. He married Rebekah, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

24.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. First draft of a long chapter: the servant retells the story in verses 34-49, so many sentences repeat verses 1-27 on purpose. Check: 'put your hand under my thigh' (verses 2 and 9) is an oath custom and is kept literally; verse 22 shekel weights are kept; verse 42 ends in a comma because the prayer continues in verse 43; verse 63 'meditate' is rendered 'to think'; verse 47 'ring on her nose' follows the Hebrew.

verses.text: Jacob went on and there were angels of God who came to Jacob.
When Jacob saw the angels, Jacob said: This is a camp of God's soldiers. Jacob named that place Mahanaim.
Jacob sent a message to his brother Esau. Esau was in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
Jacob told the men to tell his brother Esau: Sir, I am your servant Jacob and I have lived with Laban all these years.
Now I have oxen, donkeys, sheep, goats, slaves and slave women. I am sending you a message now. I want to know if you will be friendly and accept me back.
When the messengers came back to Jacob, they said to Jacob: We went to your brother Esau. Esau is coming to meet you, and Esau has 400 men with him.
Jacob became afraid and very worried. Jacob divided all the people who were with Jacob into two groups. Jacob also divided all the sheep, goats, cattle, and camels.
Jacob said: If Esau attacks one group, then the other group can flee.
Jacob prayed to God and said: God of my grandfather Abraham, God of my father Isaac, Lord, You told me to go back to my land and to my family and You said that You would be good to me.

I am not worthy but You were very good to me and You have done everything that You promised me. The first time I traveled across the Jordan River, I owned nothing but my walking stick. But now I own enough things to have two full groups.
Lord, please protect me from my brother Esau, because I am afraid of Esau. I am afraid that Esau will attack me and the women and children.
Lord, You have promised and said to me: I will be good to Jacob. I will make your descendants as many as the grains of sand of the sea. There will be so many that no one will be able to count them.
Jacob slept there that night. Jacob took some of his animals and sent a gift to his brother Esau.
Jacob's gift was 200 female goats and 20 male goats, 200 female sheep and 20 male sheep.
30 nursing camels and their calves, 40 cows and 10 bulls, and 20 female donkeys and 10 young donkeys.
Jacob gave the animals to his servants. Jacob gave a flock of animals to each servant and told the servants: Walk ahead of me, but keep each flock separate.
Jacob told his first servant: When my brother Esau comes to you and asks you whose servant you are, where you are going and whose animals these are,
you must tell Esau: Sir, they belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift that Jacob sends to you, Esau. Jacob is also coming. Jacob is behind us.

Jacob said the same to the second servant and the third servant, and to all the other servants who followed the flocks of animals. Jacob told the servants what they must say to Esau when the servants found Esau.

They also had to say to Esau: Your servant Jacob is also coming. Jacob is behind us. Jacob said to himself: I will appease Esau with this gift that goes ahead of me. Then when I see Esau face to face, maybe Esau will accept me.
Jacob first sent the gifts to Esau, and Jacob stayed that night in the camp.
Jacob got up that night. Jacob took his 2 wives, his 2 servant women and his 11 sons, and they went through the Jabbok River.
Jacob sent them through the river and then Jacob also sent his animals through the river.
Jacob stayed behind, alone. A man came and wrestled with Jacob until just before the sun came up the next day.
When the man saw that he could not defeat Jacob, the man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh, and Jacob's thigh was thrown out of joint.
The man said to Jacob: Let me go, because the sun is coming up and it is almost day. But Jacob said to the man: I will not let you go unless you bless me.
The man asked Jacob: What is your name? Jacob said: Jacob.
The man said: Your name will no longer be Jacob. From now on you will be Israel. The name Israel means: You have wrestled with God and with people, and you have won.
Jacob asked: Please tell me your name. The man said: Why do you ask what my name is? The man blessed Jacob there.
Jacob named that place Peniel. Jacob said: At this place, I saw God face to face, but my life was spared.
The sun came up when Jacob went away from Peniel. Jacob could not walk well because his thigh was hurt.
That is why the Israelites never eat the meat from the sinew in the hollow of an animal's thigh, because the man touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh.

32.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan where his father Isaac had been a stranger before.

Here is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was young, only 17 years old, Joseph looked after his father's sheep and goats with his brothers, the sons of his father's wives Bilhah and Zilpah. Joseph told his father about the bad things that his brothers did.
Jacob's other name was Israel. Jacob loved Joseph more than all of his other sons because Joseph was born when Jacob was old. Jacob gave Joseph a special coat that had many colors.
Joseph's brothers saw that their father, Jacob, loved Joseph more than them, and they hated Joseph. Joseph's brothers did not want to say anything good about Joseph.
One night Joseph dreamed and Joseph told his brothers what Joseph had dreamed. Then the brothers hated Joseph even more.
Joseph told his brothers: I dreamed a dream.
Joseph said: We were tying bundles of wheat in the field. I dreamed that my bundle of wheat was standing upright and your bundles of wheat stood around my bundle and bowed before mine.
Joseph's brothers said to Joseph: Do you really think that you will be king and rule over us? Joseph's brothers hated Joseph even more after Joseph told the brothers about the dream.
Joseph dreamed another dream and told his brothers: I dreamed again. This time the sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.

Joseph told his father and his brothers about the dream. His father rebuked Joseph and said: What kind of dream is this? Should your mother and your brothers and I come and bow down to the ground before you?
Joseph's brothers were jealous of Joseph, but Joseph's father kept the matter in mind.
Joseph's brothers had to look after their father's sheep and goats near the town of Shechem.
Jacob said to Joseph: Your brothers are looking after the sheep and goats near the town of Shechem. You must go to them. Joseph said: Yes, Father, I will go.

Jacob told Joseph: Go and see if everything is well with your brothers and with the sheep and goats. Go and look and come and tell me everything. So Jacob sent Joseph from the Hebron Valley, and Joseph went near the town of Shechem.
Joseph was walking in the field when a man saw Joseph. The man asked Joseph: What are you looking for?
Joseph said to the man: I am looking for my brothers. Do you know where they are with their sheep and goats? If you know, please tell me.
The man said: They are no longer here. They went away from here. They said that they were going to Dothan. Joseph followed his brothers and found them in Dothan.
While Joseph was still far away, the brothers saw Joseph coming. Before Joseph reached them, the brothers made a plan to kill Joseph.
Joseph's brothers said to each other: Look, here comes the big dreamer.
Joseph's brothers said: Let us kill Joseph and throw him into a pit. We can tell our father that a wild animal killed Joseph. Then we will show that all of his dreams meant nothing.
When Joseph's brothers told Reuben about it, Reuben wanted to save Joseph. Reuben said: No, we must not kill Joseph.

Reuben said to the brothers: Do not shed blood. Put Joseph into this pit in the wilderness, but do not hurt Joseph. Reuben said this so that Reuben could later rescue Joseph and bring Joseph back to their father.
When Joseph came to his brothers, they took off his coat of many colors that Joseph was wearing.
Joseph's brothers took Joseph and threw him into an empty well that was dry.

Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, then Joseph's brothers looked, and saw a group of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying many different spices, balm and myrrh. The Ishmaelites wanted to sell their spices in Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers: We will have nothing if we kill our brother Joseph and keep quiet about it.
Let us sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites. We must not kill him. Remember, Joseph is our brother. Judah's brothers agreed with Judah.
When the Midianite merchants came near, Joseph's brothers pulled Joseph out of the empty well and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for 20 pieces of silver. The merchants took Joseph to Egypt.
When Reuben came back to the empty well and saw that Joseph was not there, Reuben was very upset and tore his clothes.
Reuben went back to his brothers and asked them: The child is no longer there. Where shall I go?
Joseph's brothers killed a goat and took Joseph's coat and put blood on it.
Joseph's brothers sent Joseph's coat of many colors to their father and said: We found this coat. See if it is your son's coat or not.
Jacob looked at the coat and said: This is my son's coat. A wild animal has devoured Joseph. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.
Jacob was very sad. Jacob tore his clothes and put on sack-cloth. Jacob cried and mourned for Joseph for a long time.
All Jacob's sons and daughters came to comfort Jacob, but Jacob refused to be comforted. Jacob said: I will continue to mourn for Joseph until I die. Jacob cried a lot about Joseph.
The Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the palace guard.

37.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: People told Jacob that there was wheat in Egypt and Jacob asked his sons: Why are you sitting and just looking at each other?
The people told me that there is wheat in Egypt. My sons, you must go there and buy wheat for us so that we can have food to eat and not die from hunger.
Then 10 of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy corn.
Jacob did not send Benjamin. (Benjamin was Joseph's only full brother.) Jacob was afraid that something bad might happen to Benjamin.
So Israel's (also called Jacob) sons went with other people of Canaan to buy corn in Egypt, because there was a famine in the land of Canaan.
Joseph was the ruler of the land of Egypt, and Joseph sold the corn to the people. When Joseph's brothers came to Joseph, the brothers bowed before Joseph.

Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but Joseph pretended not to know the brothers. Joseph spoke harshly to the brothers and asked: Where do you come from? The brothers said: We come from Canaan. We have come to buy food.
Joseph knew that they were his brothers, but they did not know that he was Joseph.
Joseph remembered the dreams Joseph had dreamed about the brothers and said to the brothers: You are spies. You have come to see how you can attack our land.
The brothers said to Joseph: No, we have come to buy food.
We are all sons from one father. We are honest. We are not spies.
But Joseph said to the brothers: No, you have come to see how you can attack our land.
The brothers said: We were 12 brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Our youngest brother is still with our father, and our other brother is dead.
Joseph said to the brothers: It is like I told you. You are spies.
Joseph said, I will test you and see if what you are saying is true. You will not leave here until your youngest brother also comes here, as sure as Pharaoh lives.
One of you must go and get your brother, but the others will stay here in prison. Then I will find out if you are telling the truth or not. You are spies, as sure as Pharaoh lives.
Joseph put all the brothers in prison for 3 days.
On the 3rd day Joseph said to the brothers: I fear God. If you do what I say, I will not kill you.
If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in prison. The other brothers can go and take wheat to your hungry people at home.
Joseph said, You must then bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will believe you, and you will not die. The brothers said: Yes, we will do what you say.

The brothers said to each other: We are guilty because we did something very bad to our brother. We saw that Joseph was afraid, and Joseph begged us to help him, but we did not listen. That is why we have these problems.
Reuben said to his brothers: I told you not to do it to the child, but you did not want to listen. It is our fault that Joseph is dead.
The brothers did not realize that Joseph understood everything that they said to each other, because when the brothers talked to Joseph, someone interpreted it for Joseph.
Joseph went out and cried. Then Joseph came back and talked to the brothers. Then Joseph tied up Simeon in front of the brothers.

Joseph told the servants to fill the bags with grain. The brothers had given money for the corn, but Joseph did not keep the money. Joseph had their money put into their bags of corn. Then Joseph gave the brothers what they would need for their trip back home.
Joseph's brothers put the corn on their donkeys and they went back home.
At the lodging place, as one of Joseph's brothers opened his sack to feed his donkey, the brother saw his money in the opening of his sack.
The brother said to the other brothers: They have put my money back. Here it is in my bag. The brothers became afraid. They asked each other: What has God done to us?
The brothers went back to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan. The brothers told Jacob about everything that had happened.
The brothers said: The man who is the ruler of the land was angry when he talked to us and he put us in prison. He said that we were spies in his land.
We told him that we were honest, and we were not spies.
We told him that we were 12 brothers, all sons of the same father, and that one brother was dead and the youngest brother was with our father in Canaan.
The ruler of the land said to us: I will find out if you are honest. One of your brothers must stay here with me. Go back and take food for your hungry people at home.
But you must bring your youngest brother to me, and then I will know that you are not spies but honest people. Then I will give your brother back and you may go to any place in our land.
Jacob's sons opened their bags to take out the food, and each brother saw that his money bag with his money was in his bag. Then the brothers and their father all became afraid and they trembled.
Their father Jacob said to them: You want to take away all of my children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and you would take Benjamin from me. All these things are working against me
Reuben said to his father Jacob: Father, you may kill my 2 sons if I do not bring Benjamin back to you. Father, trust me. I will bring Benjamin back to you.

Jacob said: My son Benjamin will not go with you. Benjamin's brother is dead, and Benjamin is the only one left from that mother. If something bad happens to Benjamin on the way, I will be so sad that I will die, because I am an old man.

verses.text: The famine was very bad in that country.
The people ate all the grain they had brought from Egypt. When that grain was gone, Jacob said to his sons: Go to Egypt and buy some more grain for us to eat.
But Judah said to Jacob: The governor of that country warned us. He said: If you don't bring your brother back to me, I will refuse to talk to you.
If you send Benjamin with us, we will go down and buy grain.
But if you refuse to send Benjamin, we will not go. The man warned us to not come back without him.
Israel said: Why did you tell him you had another brother? Why did you do such a bad thing to me?

The brothers answered: The man asked lots of questions. The man wanted to know all about us and about our family. The man asked us: Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother at home? We only answered the man's questions. We didn't know the man would ask us to bring our brother to him!
Then Judah said to his father Israel: Let Benjamin go with me. I will take care of him. We have to go to Egypt to get food. If we don't go, we will all die, including our children.
I will make sure he is safe. I will be responsible for him. If I don't bring him back to you, you can blame me forever.
If you had let us go before, we could have already made two trips for food.

Then their father Israel said: If it is really true, take Benjamin with you. But take some gifts to the governor. Take some of the things we have been able to gather in our land. Take the governor some honey, pistachio nuts, almonds, spices, and myrrh.
Take twice as much money with you this time. Take the money that was given back to you after you paid last time. Maybe the governor made a mistake.
Take Benjamin and go back to the man.
I pray that God All-Powerful will make the man kind to you, so that the man will let your other brother and Benjamin come back with you. If I must lose my children, then I will lose them.
Joseph's brothers took the gifts and more money than they had the first time, and they took Benjamin with them. They went to Egypt, and they stood before Joseph.
When Joseph saw that Benjamin was with them, Joseph told the manager of his house: Bring these men to my house. Kill a cow and prepare food. They will eat with me at noon today
The man did what Joseph said, and he took Joseph's brothers to Joseph's house.

The brothers were afraid when the man took them to Joseph's house. Joseph's brothers said: It is because of the money that was in our bags the first time we came. They are bringing us here to catch us and put us in prison. We will be their slaves, and they will take our donkeys.
The brothers went to talk to the man who was the manager of Joseph's house.
The brothers said, Please, sir, we came here before to buy food.

When we came to the place where we wanted to sleep, we opened our bags and then we saw that each man's money was still in his bag. It was the money that we had paid for the corn. We have brought the money back.
We have also brought more money to buy food. We do not know who put our money back into our bags.

The manager of the house said: You must not be worried or afraid. Your God, and your father's God gave you the money in your bags. I have the money that you paid. Then the manager brought Simeon to the brothers.
The manager took the brothers to Joseph's house. The manager gave them water to wash their feet, and he gave their donkeys food
Joseph's brothers heard that they were going to eat with Joseph, so they worked until noon preparing their gifts for Joseph.
When Joseph came home, Joseph's brothers brought their gifts and then Joseph's brothers bowed down before Joseph.
Joseph asked his brothers how they were and Joseph also asked: How is your father who is so old that you told me about? Is he still alive?
Joseph's brothers answered: Our father is in good health. He is still alive. And again, Joseph's brothers bowed down before Joseph.

Then Joseph saw his brother Benjamin. (Benjamin and Joseph had the same mother.) Joseph said, Is this your youngest brother that you told me about? Then Joseph said to Benjamin, God bless you, my son!
Joseph went out of the room quickly because Joseph's heart was deeply touched over Benjamin. Joseph went into his bedroom to cry.
Joseph washed his face, and he came back. Joseph was calm again and said: Put the food on the table.

Joseph's servants seated Joseph at a table by himself. Joseph's brothers were at another table by themselves, and the Egyptians were at a table by themselves. The Egyptians believed that it was wrong for them to eat with Hebrews
Joseph's brothers were seated at a table facing Joseph. The brothers were looking at each other because, to their surprise, they had been seated in order, from the oldest to the youngest.

verses.text: Joseph told the manager of his house: Fill the men’s bags with wheat. Make it as full as they can carry and put each man’s money back into the top of his bag.
Joseph said: You must put my cup, the silver cup, in the bag of the youngest brother with his money for the corn. The manager did what Joseph told him.
Early the next morning, the brothers and their donkeys were sent back to their country.

After Joseph's brothers had left the city, Joseph said to the manager of his house, Go and follow the men. Stop them and say to them, we were good to you! So why have you been bad to us? Why did you steal my master's silver cup?
My master drinks from that cup, and he uses it to learn secret things. What you did was wrong!
The manager went out to the brothers and stopped them. The manager told them what Joseph had said
The brothers asked the manager of the house: Why does the governor say these things? We would never do a bad thing like that.
The brothers said: We brought back the money that we found in our bags before. We would never steal silver or gold from your master's house.
If you find the cup in one of our bags, you may kill that person and then we will all be your slaves.
The manager said: Yes, we will do as you say. But only the man in whose bag I find the cup will be my slave. All the other brothers may go.
Everyone put his bag on the ground quickly and opened it
The manager looked into the bags. The manager started looking in the bag of the oldest brother and stopped at the youngest brother, and then the manager found the cup in Benjamin's bag
The brothers tore their clothes because they were sad and upset. They put everything they had on their donkeys and went back to the city.
When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, Joseph was still there. Judah and his brothers lay before Joseph with their faces to the ground.
Joseph asked the brothers: What have you done? You must know that a man like me can tell what will happen in the future.

Judah said to Joseph: Sir, what can we say to you? What can we say and how can we prove that we are innocent? God has shown that we are guilty. Sir, here we are now. We are your slaves, all of us, and the one who had your cup.
Joseph said: No, I would never do that. The man who had my cup will be my slave. The others may go back to your father.
Judah came to Joseph and said to Joseph: Please, sir, may I talk to you alone? Do not get angry with me. You are like Pharaoh.
Sir, when we were here the first time, you asked us if we had a father and a brother.

And we answered you, we have a father—he is an old man. And we have a younger brother. Our father loves him because he was born while our father was old. This youngest son's full brother is dead, so this youngest son is the only son left from that mother. Our father loves him very much
Sir, you told us to bring our youngest brother to you because you wanted to see him.
Sir, we told you: That young boy cannot come. He cannot leave his father. If his father loses him, his father will be so sad that he will die
But, sir, you told us if we did not bring our youngest brother with us, then we could not see you again.
We went to our father, and we told him what you said
One day our father told us that we would have to go and buy food,
But we said: We cannot go down unless our youngest brother is with us. We are not allowed to see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.
Our father told us: You know that I had only 2 children with this wife.
I let one son go away, and he was killed by a wild animal. And I haven't seen him since.
If you take this son away from me and something happens to him, then I, an old man, will be so sad that I will die.
Now, imagine what will happen when we go home to the father without our youngest brother—he is the most important thing in our father's life!
My father will die if he sees his son is not with us. Then it will be our fault if our father who is old dies because he is so sad.
I promised my father that I would look after his son and make sure that he was safe. I said if he did not go back to my father, then it would be my fault forever.
Sir, please let me stay here in my brother's place. Sir, I will be your slave, but please let the boy go back with his brothers.
I cannot go back to my father if the boy is not with me. I am very afraid of what would happen to my father.

44.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by the nouns they refer to and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.
